s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with exertional worsening and relief with forward leaning, accompanied by shortness of breath and signs of cardiac involvement
salient_findings: Sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Malar rash and jugular venous distension
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration
key_facts: 44-year-old woman presented to the emergency department
2 days of sharp, stabbing right-sided chest pain (8/10)
Pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward
Shortness of breath on minimal activity
Chronic right lower-leg swelling
Six months of symmetric wrist stiffness that improved during the day
History of heavy menstrual bleeding and a miscarriage at age 14
Chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses
Placement of a nonretrievable inferior vena cava filter
Obese and mildly tachypneic on examination
Vital signs: temperature 98.6°F, blood pressure 116/91 mm Hg, heart rate 88/min, respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
Malar rash and jugular venous distension on examination
Tender anterior chest wall and bibasilar Velcro crackles on examination
Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration on examination
Hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, platelets 71 × 10^3/mm^3, ESR 55 mm/h, CRP 90.9 mg/L, D-dimer 3.7 µg/mL, and prolonged PTT of 49 s with normal PT/INR/fibrinogen on laboratory studies

shortlist.label: Acute Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Sharp, stabbing chest pain worsened by exertion and relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by pericardial effusion on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and elevated ESR and CRP levels, suggesting a systemic autoimmune disorder

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent deep vein thromboses, miscarriage, and prolonged PTT, suggesting a hypercoagulable state

shortlist.label: Tricuspid Regurgitation
shortlist.why_kept: Grade 2/6 pansystolic murmur at the left sternal border that increased with inspiration, and tricuspid valve vegetation on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Tricuspid valve vegetation on echocardiography, and history of chronic warfarin-refractory deep vein thromboses, suggesting a hypercoagulable state

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of sharp chest pain, shortness of breath, malar rash, symmetric wrist stiffness, and laboratory findings of low hemoglobin, low platelets, elevated ESR, and CRP are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). The presence of a malar rash, a classic symptom of SLE, along with other systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute Pericarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has chest pain and a pericardial effusion, the presence of other systemic symptoms and laboratory findings are more consistent with SLE.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of deep vein thromboses and a nonretrievable inferior vena cava filter, the presence of other systemic symptoms and laboratory findings are more consistent with SLE.

rejected.label: Tricuspid Regurgitation
rejected.why: Tricuspid regurgitation is a finding on the patient's echocardiogram, but it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the patient's overall presentation.

rejected.label: Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis
rejected.why: While the patient has vegetations on the tricuspid valve, the presence of other systemic symptoms and laboratory findings are more consistent with SLE.
